correctness.rationale: The exact marked recurrence E[C_{j+1}^{rising r} z^{Delta H}|C_j]=C_j^{rising r}(p+(1-p)z+rp/j) yields formula (1) by coefficient extraction. Moment-order-r exponential tilting yields independent Bernoulli variables q_j=(1-p)/(1+rp/j), with mean h-O(log n) and variance Np(1-p)+O(log n). A uniform lattice local CLT proved via characteristic functions gives the exact probability ratio tending to one at h. Uniform gamma ratios, lower-moment polynomial induction and Carleman establish all ordinary moments and the unique Mittag–Leffler limit for all p_n→p∈(0,1). Endpoint finite identities agree with the model. Independently enumerated recursive parents and deletion masks and rational polynomial expansions produced 3359 passing finite assertions; finite checks are not infinite proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The alternative model is a Simon-type Chinese restaurant process conditioned on exactly h innovations, equivalently random recursive-tree bond percolation conditioned on exactly h deleted edges, or a uniformly chosen subset of h closed edges. originality.rationale: The candidate is a fixed-count (hypergeometric) edge-deletion theorem. Zheng (arXiv:2606.01881, June 2026) and Desmarais–Holmgren–Wagner (arXiv:2110.15050) treat independently retained edges; the latter already establishes the canonical Mittag–Leffler root-cluster limit and is explicitly credited. Kürsten gives canonical moments, and Baur chiefly considers p(n) approaching one. The new all-r microcanonical formula follows coefficient extraction, and the substantive distinct conclusion is the relative Poisson-binomial local limit under conditioning on a binomial event with probability Θ(n^{-1/2}), yielding a whole non-Gaussian limit for arbitrary moving fractions. Direct published-finding corpus searches and comparisons to relevant published cluster joint results identified no theorem whose stated result implies this exact-conditioned limit. The possibility that a general unindexed conditional local-limit theorem subsumes the argument remains a material historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: A more general unindexed theorem concerning local ensemble equivalence for strongly reinforced or regularly varying stochastic recursions might imply the conditional limit.
Some historical papers on fixed-count mutations in Yule–Simon processes may use different terminology and remain uninspected.

value.rationale: The mathematical question asks whether a non-Gaussian, strongly path-dependent root-cluster law survives imposing a global exact extensive edge-deletion budget. Conditioning on a binomial point event of order N^{-1/2} is not controlled by the known weak Bernoulli limit. The explicit all-order fixed-budget moment identity and tilted local-limit mechanism solve this natural constrained random-forest problem for every deterministic fixed-budget sequence with p_n→p, including arbitrarily slowly drifting fractions. Such an ensemble-invariance result is relevant to tree fragmentation with prescribed numbers of components, and concerns the complete root-cluster law, not an arbitrary slice or routine mean computation.
